sections.title: باب 3 — متن (7)

paras.text: (continued from p.51) … this is not possible; rather there are some restrictions on creating credit money.
paras.urdu: (ص 51 سے جاری) … میں ایسا ممکن نہیں بلکہ اعتباری زر پیدا کرنے پر کچھ بندشیں ہیں۔
paras.pashto: (له ۵۱ مخ دوام) … دا شونې نه ده، بلکې د اعتباري پیسو پر پیدا کولو ځینې بندیزونه شته.

paras.text: 1. Need for Cash
paras.urdu: 1۔ نقد روپیہ کی ضرورت: (Need for Cash)
paras.pashto: 1. نغدو پیسو ته اړتیا (Need for Cash)

paras.text: Although all the people to whom the bank gives loans do not demand rupees from the bank in the form of cash, still for daily needs they require “cash rupees”. Therefore the bank cannot create credit money beyond a certain limit, because the more credit money it creates, the more the need for cash will also increase. And since the money with the bank is not unlimited, it cannot issue unlimited credit money either. While explaining the process of creating money we had assumed that all receipts and payments take place through cheques, whereas in reality this does not happen; rather cash too is used.
paras.urdu: اگرچہ تمام لوگ جنہیں بینک قرضہ دیتا ہے نقدی کی صورت میں بینک سے روپیہ طلب نہیں کرتے پھر بھی روزمرہ کی ضروریات کے لیے انہیں ”نقد روپیہ“ درکار رہتا ہے۔ لہٰذا بینک ایک خاص حد سے زیادہ اعتباری زر پیدا نہیں کر سکتا۔ کیونکہ جتنا اعتباری زر پیدا کرے گا اتنی ہی نقدی کی ضرورت بھی بڑھتی جائے گی۔ اور چونکہ بینک کے پاس زر لامحدود نہیں ہوتا اس لیے وہ اعتباری زر بھی لامحدود جاری نہیں کر سکتا۔ تخلیقِ زر کا عمل واضح کرتے ہوئے ہم نے فرض کر لیا تھا کہ تمام وصولیاں اور ادائیگیاں چیکوں کے ذریعے ہوتی ہیں۔ حالانکہ درحقیقت ایسا نہیں ہوتا بلکہ نقدی بھی استعمال ہوتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: که څه هم ټول هغه خلک چې بانک ورته پور ورکوي، له بانک په نغده بڼه پیسې نه غواړي، خو بیا هم د ورځنیو اړتیاوو لپاره ورته ”نغدې پیسې“ په کار وي. نو بانک له یوې ټاکلې اندازې زیاتې اعتباري پیسې نه شي پیدا کولی، ځکه څومره چې اعتباري پیسې پیدا کړي، هومره به نغدو ته اړتیا هم زیاتېږي. او څرنګه چې د بانک پیسې نامحدودې نه دي، نو اعتباري پیسې هم نامحدودې نه شي جاري کولی. د پیسو د پیدا کولو د عمل د روښانه کولو پر وخت موږ فرض کړې وه چې ټولې وصولۍ او تادیې د چکونو له لارې کېږي، حال دا چې په حقیقت کې داسې نه کېږي، بلکې نغدې هم کارېږي.

paras.text: 2. Deficiency of Securities
paras.urdu: 2۔ ضمانتوں کی قلت: (Deficiency of Securities)
paras.pashto: 2. د ضمانتونو کمښت (Deficiency of Securities)

paras.text: While giving loans to people the bank demands securities from them, e.g. property, gold, silver, jewellery and bonds etc.; these are all different forms of wealth. Therefore the bank does not create money from itself, but gives money in exchange for wealth and securities. As it were, it changes the different forms of wealth (which are relatively less transferable) into cash money and credit money. And since people have limited property or possessions to give as security, the bank too can create credit money only up to that limit.
paras.urdu: بینک لوگوں کو قرضہ دیتے وقت ان سے ضمانتیں طلب کرتا ہے مثلاً جائیداد، سونا، چاندی، زیورات اور بانڈ وغیرہ، یہ سب دولت کی مختلف صورتیں ہیں۔ لہٰذا بینک اپنے پاس سے زر پیدا نہیں کرتا۔ بلکہ دولت اور ضمانتوں کے عوض زر دیتا ہے۔ گویا دولت کی مختلف صورتوں کو (جو مقابلتاً کم انتقال پذیر ہوتی ہے لے کر انہیں) نقدی زر اعتباری زر سے میں بدل دیتا ہے۔ اور چونکہ لوگوں کے پاس ضمانت کے طور پر دینے کے لیے جائیداد یا املاک محدود ہیں۔ اس لیے بینک بھی اسی حد تک ہی اعتباری زر پیدا کر سکتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: بانک خلکو ته د پور ورکولو پر وخت ترې ضمانتونه غواړي؛ لکه ملکیت، سره زر، سپین زر، ګاڼې او بانډونه او نور؛ دا ټول د شتمنۍ بېلابېلې بڼې دي. نو بانک له ځانه پیسې نه پیدا کوي، بلکې د شتمنۍ او ضمانتونو په بدل کې پیسې ورکوي. ګواکې د شتمنۍ بېلابېلې بڼې (چې په پرتله یې لږ لېږدېدونکې دي) په نغدو او اعتباري پیسو بدلوي. او څرنګه چې د خلکو سره د ضمانت لپاره ملکیت یا جایداد محدود دی، نو بانک هم تر همدې اندازې اعتباري پیسې پیدا کولی شي.

paras.text: Professor Crowther:
paras.urdu: پروفیسر کراؤتھر:
paras.pashto: پروفېسر کراوتر:

paras.text: “Banks do not create money out of the air; rather they give the different forms of wealth the form of money.”
paras.urdu: ”بینک ہوا میں سے زر پیدا نہیں کر لیتے بلکہ دولت کی مختلف شکلوں کو زر کی شکل دے دیتے ہیں۔“
paras.pashto: ”بانکونه له هوا پیسې نه پیدا کوي، بلکې د شتمنۍ بېلابېلو بڼو ته د پیسو بڼه ورکوي.“

paras.text: 3. Policy of Central Bank
paras.urdu: 3۔ مرکزی بینک کی پالیسی: (Policy of Central Bank)
paras.pashto: 3. د مرکزي بانک پالیسي (Policy of Central Bank)

paras.text: The central bank too imposes some restrictions on creating credit money. This bank, in view of the economic and financial conditions of the country, keeps taking some steps in connection with increasing or decreasing the quantity of credit money. Therefore commercial banks are not completely free in connection with creating credit money.
paras.urdu: اعتباری زر پیدا کرنے پر مرکزی بینک بھی کچھ پابندیاں عائد کر دیتا ہے۔ یہ بینک ملک کے معاشی اور مالی حالات کے پیشِ نظر اعتباری زر کی مقدار بڑھانے یا گھٹانے کے سلسلے میں بعض اقدامات کرتا رہتا ہے۔ لہٰذا تجارتی بینک اعتباری زر پیدا کرنے کے سلسلے میں مکمل طور پر آزاد نہیں ہوتے۔
paras.pashto: د اعتباري پیسو پر پیدا کولو مرکزي بانک هم ځینې بندیزونه لګوي. دا بانک د هېواد د اقتصادي او مالي حالاتو په پام کې نیولو سره د اعتباري پیسو د مقدار د زیاتولو یا کمولو په برخه کې ځینې ګامونه پورته کوي. نو سوداګریز بانکونه د اعتباري پیسو د پیدا کولو په برخه کې بشپړ ازاد نه دي.

paras.text: 4. Shortage of borrowers (Unavailasility of Borrowers)
paras.urdu: 4۔ قرض داروں کی قلت: (Unavailasility of Borrowers)
paras.pashto: 4. د پور اخیستونکو کمښت (Unavailasility of Borrowers)

paras.text: For giving and taking loans the existence of two parties is necessary: the lender, i.e. the bank, may be ready to give a loan, but there may be nobody (trader or industrialist) present to take it. This situation especially arises in times of depression and economic crisis, because in such a condition prices begin to fall, demand decreases, opportunities of investment become few, and people stop taking loans from banks. Therefore in such a situation too the bank cannot create credit money. In short, for creating credit money the existence of four things is necessary.
paras.urdu: قرضہ دینے اور لینے کے لیے دو فریقوں کا ہونا ضروری ہے کہ قرضہ دینے والا یعنی بینک تو قرضہ دینے کے لیے تیار ہو، لیکن اسے لینے کے لیے کوئی (تاجر یا صنعت کار) موجود نہ ہو۔ یہ صورت خاص طور پر سرد بازاری اور معاشی بحران کے زمانہ میں پیدا ہوتی ہے کیونکہ ایسے حالت میں قیمتیں گرنا شروع ہو جاتی ہیں۔ طلب گھٹ جاتی ہے۔ سرمایہ کاری کے مواقع کم ہو جاتے ہیں۔ اور لوگ بینکوں سے قرضہ لینا بند کر دیتے ہیں۔ لہٰذا ایسی صورت میں بھی بینک اعتباری زر پیدا نہیں کر سکتے۔ غرضیکہ اعتباری زر پیدا کرنے کے لیے چار باتوں کا ہونا ضروری ہے۔
paras.pashto: د پور ورکولو او اخیستلو لپاره د دوو خواوو شتون اړین دی: پور ورکوونکی یعنې بانک پور ورکولو ته تیار وي، خو د اخیستلو لپاره یې څوک (سوداګر یا صنعتکار) موجود نه وي. دا حالت په ځانګړي ډول د رکود او اقتصادي بحران په وخت کې پیدا کېږي، ځکه په داسې حالت کې بیې راټیټېږي، غوښتنه کمېږي، د پانګونې فرصتونه لږېږي او خلک له بانکونو پور اخیستل بندوي. نو په داسې حالت کې هم بانکونه اعتباري پیسې نه شي پیدا کولی. لنډه دا چې د اعتباري پیسو د پیدا کولو لپاره د څلورو خبرو شتون اړین دی.

paras.text: i. The bank should receive cash from somewhere as a deposit.
paras.urdu: i۔ بینک کو کہیں سے نقد رقم بطور امانت وصول ہو۔
paras.pashto: i. بانک ته دې له کوم ځایه نغدې پیسې د امانت په توګه ورسېږي.

paras.text: ii. The bank should be willing to give loans.
paras.urdu: ii۔ بینک قرضہ دینے پر آمادہ ہو۔
paras.pashto: ii. بانک دې پور ورکولو ته چمتو وي.

paras.text: iii. Business people should be ready to take loans.
paras.urdu: iii۔ کاروباری لوگ قرضہ لینے پر تیار ہوں۔
paras.pashto: iii. سوداګر دې پور اخیستلو ته تیار وي.

paras.text: iv. The borrower should not insist on taking cash, but be satisfied with a cheque.
paras.urdu: iv۔ قرضہ لینے والا نقدی لینے پر اصرار نہ کرے بلکہ چیک پر ہی مطمئن ہو جائے۔

sections.theory:
(continued from p.51) … this is not possible; rather there are some restrictions on creating credit money.

1. Need for Cash

Although all the people to whom the bank gives loans do not demand rupees from the bank in the form of cash, still for daily needs they require “cash rupees”. Therefore the bank cannot create credit money beyond a certain limit, because the more credit money it creates, the more the need for cash will also increase. And since the money with the bank is not unlimited, it cannot issue unlimited credit money either. While explaining the process of creating money we had assumed that all receipts and payments take place through cheques, whereas in reality this does not happen; rather cash too is used.

2. Deficiency of Securities

While giving loans to people the bank demands securities from them, e.g. property, gold, silver, jewellery and bonds etc.; these are all different forms of wealth. Therefore the bank does not create money from itself, but gives money in exchange for wealth and securities. As it were, it changes the different forms of wealth (which are relatively less transferable) into cash money and credit money. And since people have limited property or possessions to give as security, the bank too can create credit money only up to that limit.

Professor Crowther:

“Banks do not create money out of the air; rather they give the different forms of wealth the form of money.”

3. Policy of Central Bank

The central bank too imposes some restrictions on creating credit money. This bank, in view of the economic and financial conditions of the country, keeps taking some steps in connection with increasing or decreasing the quantity of credit money. Therefore commercial banks are not completely free in connection with creating credit money.

4. Shortage of borrowers (Unavailasility of Borrowers)

For giving and taking loans the existence of two parties is necessary: the lender, i.e. the bank, may be ready to give a loan, but there may be nobody (trader or industrialist) present to take it. This situation especially arises in times of depression and economic crisis, because in such a condition prices begin to fall, demand decreases, opportunities of investment become few, and people stop taking loans from banks. Therefore in such a situation too the bank cannot create credit money. In short, for creating credit money the existence of four things is necessary.

i. The bank should receive cash from somewhere as a deposit.

ii. The bank should be willing to give loans.

iii. Business people should be ready to take loans.

iv. The borrower should not insist on taking cash, but be satisfied with a cheque.

sections.content:
(continued from p.51) … this is not possible; rather there are some restrictions on creating credit money.

1. Need for Cash

Although all the people to whom the bank gives loans do not demand rupees from the bank in the form of cash, still for daily needs they require “cash rupees”. Therefore the bank cannot create credit money beyond a certain limit, because the more credit money it creates, the more the need for cash will also increase. And since the money with the bank is not unlimited, it cannot issue unlimited credit money either. While explaining the process of creating money we had assumed that all receipts and payments take place through cheques, whereas in reality this does not happen; rather cash too is used.

2. Deficiency of Securities

While giving loans to people the bank demands securities from them, e.g. property, gold, silver, jewellery and bonds etc.; these are all different forms of wealth. Therefore the bank does not create money from itself, but gives money in exchange for wealth and securities. As it were, it changes the different forms of wealth (which are relatively less transferable) into cash money and credit money. And since people have limited property or possessions to give as security, the bank too can create credit money only up to that limit.

Professor Crowther:

“Banks do not create money out of the air; rather they give the different forms of wealth the form of money.”

3. Policy of Central Bank

The central bank too imposes some restrictions on creating credit money. This bank, in view of the economic and financial conditions of the country, keeps taking some steps in connection with increasing or decreasing the quantity of credit money. Therefore commercial banks are not completely free in connection with creating credit money.

4. Shortage of borrowers (Unavailasility of Borrowers)

For giving and taking loans the existence of two parties is necessary: the lender, i.e. the bank, may be ready to give a loan, but there may be nobody (trader or industrialist) present to take it. This situation especially arises in times of depression and economic crisis, because in such a condition prices begin to fall, demand decreases, opportunities of investment become few, and people stop taking loans from banks. Therefore in such a situation too the bank cannot create credit money. In short, for creating credit money the existence of four things is necessary.

i. The bank should receive cash from somewhere as a deposit.

ii. The bank should be willing to give loans.

iii. Business people should be ready to take loans.

iv. The borrower should not insist on taking cash, but be satisfied with a cheque.

Instruments of Credit

Credit means trust or reliance: that the lender (Lender) relies upon the borrower (Borrower) and considers that the debtor will return the loan after a fixed period, or will pay the price of the goods he has bought. In other words, taking and giving loans, or giving and taking goods on credit instead of cash buying and selling, is called credit (Credit). There are three kinds of credit.

Types of Credit

There are three kinds of credit, which are as follows: i. consumer credit, ii. trade credit, iii. bank credit.

i. Consumers Credit

The loan or credit which common shopkeepers or financial institutions give to consumers and the public for the purchase of consumer goods is called consumers’ loan or consumer credit.

ii. Trade Credit

By this is meant that loan which is given to factory owners for providing raw material, or which factory owners provide to wholesalers or retailers.

iii. Bank Credit

By this is meant that credit or lending which a bank gives to its customers in the form of loans (Loan) or overdraft (Over Draft) (i.e. giving a sum in loan in excess of the customer’s deposited deposit).

While taking or giving a loan a written promise is made. It has many forms, which are called instruments of credit money. Their kinds are as follows.

1. Book Credit

When a customer buys some goods from a shopkeeper on credit, the shopkeeper makes its entry in his accounts. After some period the customer returns the sum to the shopkeeper and the account is settled. Transactions of this kind are called book credit. Usually students resident in the hostel too take tea and toast on credit from the college canteen, and on the first date of every month (when the money order comes from home) settle the bill.

2. Promissory Note

By this is meant such a promise which the debtor makes in writing with his creditor (Lender), and in which he makes this explanation that he will pay this sum to the creditor after the passing of a particular period. This promise of a sum is also called a promissory note.
